classification.difficultyReason: Without replacement with three categories. Each part needs the 'exactly k of a type' case, with its orderings counted and the other draws grouped as 'not that type'. Two parts, but the same structure.

content.prompt: A bag contains nine lollies, all of identical appearance: four raspberry, three lime and two lemon. Kim randomly selects and eats three lollies from the bag. Find the probability that:

children.label: a
children.prompt: Kim eats exactly two raspberry lollies,

answer.worked:
Let R mean raspberry and N mean not raspberry. The orders RRN, RNR and NRR have equal probabilities.

$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{exactly two raspberry})&=3\times\frac{4}{9}\times\frac{3}{8}\times\frac{5}{7}\\P(\text{exactly two raspberry})&=\frac{180}{504}\\P(\text{exactly two raspberry})&=\frac{5}{14}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Kim eats exactly one lime lollie.

answer.worked:
Let L mean lime and N mean not lime. The orders LNN, NLN and NNL have equal probabilities.

$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{exactly one lime})&=3\times\frac{3}{9}\times\frac{6}{8}\times\frac{5}{7}\\P(\text{exactly one lime})&=\frac{270}{504}\\P(\text{exactly one lime})&=\frac{15}{28}\end{aligned}$$
